examples.name: Baked Cod with Lemon and Greens
instructions: Preheat a conventional oven to 200°C. Use fresh or fully thawed cod and pat it dry; place it in a small baking dish.
Coat the cod with about half the olive oil, the lemon juice and the salt.
Bake for about 12-15 minutes; a thick fillet may need longer. Check the fish in its thickest part using the fish cooking check below before serving.
While the fish bakes, warm the remaining oil in a frying pan over medium heat. Add the spinach and stir for about 2-3 minutes until wilted.
Plate the cod with the spinach and spoon over the juices from the baking dish.
examples.whyItHelps: Cod is a lean source of protein and iron, and spinach adds anti-inflammatory antioxidants and vitamin K.
examples.freshOrFrozen: Spinach: frozen works well once thawed and squeezed dry; use fresh if serving barely wilted.

examples.name: Beef and Veggie Skillet
instructions: Dice the onion and bell pepper; wash and dry the spinach.
Heat the olive oil in a frying pan over medium heat. Add the onion and pepper and stir for about 4-5 minutes until starting to soften.
Add the ground beef and break it into small pieces with a spatula. Cook for about 6-8 minutes, stirring regularly.
Check the ground beef using the ground-meat cooking check below; continue cooking if needed.
Stir in the spinach for about 1-2 minutes until wilted, then serve hot.
examples.whyItHelps: Lean beef is a strong source of iron, and bell pepper and spinach add anti-inflammatory vitamins and antioxidants.
examples.freshOrFrozen: Bell pepper: both work, frozen sliced pepper is fine cooked into a skillet. Spinach: frozen works well once thawed and squeezed dry.
examples.colorPalette: Browned beef with red bell pepper and wilted green spinach

examples.name: Chicken Rice Soup
instructions: Use chicken and rice that have already been fully cooked. Peel and finely dice the carrot; cut or shred the cooked chicken.
Bring the stock to a boil in a saucepan. Add the carrot, reduce to a gentle simmer and cook for about 8-10 minutes until tender.
Stir in the cooked chicken and rice. Simmer for about 3-5 minutes, stirring, until the soup is hot throughout.
Check the reheating guidance below for chilled cooked ingredients; serve immediately once they are thoroughly reheated.
examples.whyItHelps: Chicken and stock provide protein and iron, and carrot adds a mild dose of fiber and beta-carotene.
examples.freshOrFrozen: Carrot: both work, frozen sliced carrot is fine in soups; fresh is better where texture matters.
examples.colorPalette: Golden broth with pale chicken, rice, and orange carrot

examples.name: Overnight Oats with Chia and Berries
instructions: Stir the rolled oats, chia seeds, milk and Greek yogurt together in a covered jar or bowl.
Refrigerate for at least 8 hours or overnight; stir again after about 15 minutes if convenient to disperse chia clumps.
Wash fresh berries or prepare frozen berries according to their packet.
Stir the oats before eating, add the berries and serve chilled. Overnight chilling is additional to the hands-on preparation time.
examples.whyItHelps: Oats and chia seeds together deliver a strong dose of fiber, and berries add anti-inflammatory antioxidants.
examples.vegetableSubstitutes: Mixed berries → any frozen berry mix
examples.freshOrFrozen: Berries: fresh or frozen both work well as a topping, straight from the freezer is fine.

examples.name: Lentil Soup with Turmeric and Ginger
instructions: Use dried red split lentils for these timings; rinse them. Dice the onion and carrot and grate the ginger.
Cook the onion, carrot and ginger in a saucepan over medium heat with a few tablespoons of the measured broth for about 3-4 minutes.
Add the lentils, turmeric and remaining broth, bring to a gentle boil and lower the heat.
Simmer for about 20-25 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the lentils are soft; add water if needed.
Finish with the parsley and serve hot.
examples.whyItHelps: Lentils are high in fiber and plant protein; turmeric and ginger are traditional anti-inflammatory spices used in many cuisines.
examples.vegetableSubstitutes: Carrot → parsnip or sweet potato; Onion → shallot or leek
examples.freshOrFrozen: Carrot: Both work. Frozen sliced or diced carrot is fine in soups, stews, and curries; fresh is better for raw or roasted dishes where texture matters. Onion: Frozen diced onion works fine in any cooked dish; use fresh for raw uses like salads or garnish.

examples.name: Turkey Chili with Kidney Beans, Bell Peppers, and Avocado
instructions: Use canned kidney beans, drained and rinsed; dice the pepper, tomato and avocado.
Brown the ground turkey in a non-stick saucepan over medium heat for about 6-8 minutes, breaking up clumps.
Add the beans, pepper, tomato, chili powder and cumin with a splash of water if needed. Bring to a gentle simmer.
Simmer on low for about 20 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the pepper is tender. Check the turkey using the poultry cooking check below.
Serve topped with the avocado and cilantro.
examples.whyItHelps: Lean ground turkey combined with fiber-rich beans and vitamin-C-rich peppers.
examples.vegetableSubstitutes: Bell pepper → poblano pepper or zucchini; Tomato → red bell pepper or sun-dried tomato
examples.freshOrFrozen: Bell pepper: Frozen sliced peppers work well in any cooked dish (stir-fries, curries, stews, roasting); use fresh if it needs to stay raw or crisp. Tomato: Fresh is better for salads and raw preparations; frozen or canned diced tomato is fine in anything cooked (sauces, soups, stews).
